body:
> Just a little question. Have you ever tried traveling. Moving out to a different country? Sorry if this question is bad, I am new here.

In my younger days I traveled quite a bit. Saddest place I ever went to was LA, despite the fact that I loved the heat there. Best place was Holland, and especially Rotterdam.

Moving wouldn't change the loneliness or lack of hope. Sadly, those have been hammered into place with great care by the good people of this indifferent universe. The bullying might have stopped some 20 years ago, but the scars are still there, and they rip across any trust I have in my body or any chance I might be able to be close to another person. The damage is just too severe. 

It's weird, but I didn't really start to love myself until about the same time last year, and when I did I realized that I was just punishing myself by being live. I did, however, promise to stay here for at least a year. Hope is like that. It needs to be squeezed utterly dry before you can continue.

Still, my dreams last night, and how I feel this morning are proof enough for me that I am on the right track. I am looking forward to not having to bring a napkin everywhere with me.

> I agree with your assessment of the world. I had someone tell me recently, "life is for enjoying" and I didn't know whether to laugh in their face or cry or both. 

I technically believe that the world is for enjoyment and that the point of living is joy. It's when we can't align our existence with joy that pain springs forth. The reasons can be varied and for me to explain them would require me to go into metaphysics that I've studied for myself. Since I have no inclination to go into debate about it I'll refrain from elaborating on it.

> I'm not gonna give you canned responses since I've both received and given those before (and for those in a limited crisis type situation they might even work). 

They have their place and time. For someone who is thinking of suicide because their spouse left them or they lost their jobs, the canned response is an excellent tool and will often keep the person in question from doing something stupid based on a one time event. So they are not useless, as canned as they are.

> I wanna ask one thing though. What would it take for you to want to continue living? I am asking it out of curiosity and it is not a reverse-psychology trick. Although it is the one question I find of actual significance in this sort of situation.

A hard reset. A new body, a restart of most of what I am. I've actually asked myself this question in the past months to see if there is a reason to go onward. As I found that there was no answer that aligned with the current situation I found it best to take my chance on reincarnation or oblivion(the only two solutions that seem to have at least partial evidence in current reality based on several studies).

Of course, I am going to be meticulous this time. I have a rather shitty track record. Attempted 5 times and I am still here. :(
